seoTitle: How to Add eBay Authenticity Guarantee in 2026 Guide
metaDescription: Selling sneakers, watches, or handbags on eBay? Here's how Authenticity Guarantee works, which category rules apply, and how the badge appears to buyers.
intro: eBay's Authenticity Guarantee puts eBay's own inspection process behind certain high-value listings — sneakers, handbags, watches, jewelry, and streetwear — and marks qualifying items with a checkmark buyers can see right in search results. This guide follows the actual eBay pages that make up the program: the landing page that explains it, the category breakdown showing which item types qualify, and what the badge actually looks like once it's attached to a live listing. It's aimed at sellers in these categories who want the trust boost the badge provides, and who need to understand what qualifying and shipping through authentication actually involves before listing.

steps.heading: Understand what Authenticity Guarantee actually covers
steps.body: The Authenticity Guarantee landing page frames the program in one line — real items, checked by real experts — and eBay is explicit in the footer that the program runs independently of the brands themselves; it's eBay's own authentication service, not a manufacturer partnership. The page sits under its own section of eBay's site, reachable from the main search and category navigation, and functions as both an explainer for buyers and a directory of what's currently eligible. Before listing anything, this page is worth reading in full, since it lays out the checkmark buyers will eventually see on your listing and what it's actually certifying.

image.caption: eBay's Authenticity Guarantee landing page: "Real sneakers. Checked by real experts," with a note that the program is independent from, and not associated with, any of the brands sold.

steps.heading: Check which category your item falls under
steps.body: Authenticity Guarantee isn't one blanket program — it's organized by category, with Sneakers, Handbags, Watches, Jewelry, and Streetwear each having their own eligibility rules, price thresholds, and authentication process. Picking the correct category when you list matters more here than in an ordinary eBay listing, since the wrong category can mean your item never enters the authentication pipeline even if it would otherwise qualify. If you sell across more than one of these categories, it's worth checking each one's specific requirements separately rather than assuming they all work the same way.

image.caption: Authenticity Guarantee's category breakdown — Sneakers, Handbags, Watches, Jewelry, and Streetwear each link to their own eligibility and process details.

steps.heading: Meet the price and condition requirements
steps.body: Each category sets its own minimum price for Authenticity Guarantee eligibility, and items below that threshold simply won't route through the authentication process regardless of how the listing is set up. Condition matters too — heavily worn or modified items are more likely to face scrutiny or rejection during inspection, so an honest, accurate listing description upfront reduces the chance of a failed authentication after a buyer has already paid.

steps.heading: List with shipping set up for authentication routing
steps.body: Once a buyer purchases an item enrolled in Authenticity Guarantee, it doesn't ship straight to them — it routes through eBay's authentication center first, gets inspected by a specialist in that category, and only then continues on to the buyer. Your listing's shipping settings need to support this routing, which generally means using eBay-recommended shipping labels or services rather than an entirely custom arrangement that could interfere with the item reaching the authentication center correctly.

steps.heading: See how the badge appears once your listing qualifies
steps.body: Once your listing meets the program's requirements, the Authenticity Guarantee checkmark appears directly under the price in search results, visible to buyers before they even click into the listing, alongside seller-set details like Buy It Now or Best Offer. This visibility is the actual mechanism behind the sales lift sellers report from the program — buyers comparing several similar listings can see at a glance which ones come with third-party verification, which matters especially in categories with a lot of counterfeit risk like sneakers and handbags.

image.caption: Search results for New Balance sneakers, with an Authenticity Guarantee checkmark shown directly under several listings — buyers see this badge before they ever open the item page.

steps.heading: Track the item through authentication after a sale
steps.body: After a sale, the tracking information you'll see reflects two shipping legs rather than one — from you to eBay's authentication center, and then from there to the buyer once the item passes inspection. This adds a few extra days to overall delivery time compared to a direct shipment, which is worth mentioning in your listing description so buyers aren't surprised by the longer timeline, and it's also why response time on your first shipping leg matters more than usual.

faq.question: What items qualify for eBay's Authenticity Guarantee?
faq.answer: The program applies to high-value categories like sneakers, handbags, watches, jewelry, and streetwear, provided the specific listing meets that category's price and condition requirements.

faq.question: Who pays for the authentication process?
faq.answer: eBay's fee structure for Authenticity Guarantee varies by category, so check the current fees listed on the program's category pages before pricing a listing.

faq.question: Does the Authenticity Guarantee badge help with sales?
faq.answer: Yes — the checkmark appears directly in search results next to the price, letting buyers compare verified and unverified listings at a glance, which is designed to boost buyer trust and visibility.

faq.question: Does Authenticity Guarantee reduce disputes and returns?
faq.answer: Yes, because eBay's authentication center inspects the item before it reaches the buyer, which is designed to reduce return disputes and fraud on high-value listings.
